$comment: Cross-language conformance fixture for which header a request's auth writes when the request already carries one (issue #2475). Read by BOTH the engine gtest suite (engine/tests/auth_header_precedence_test.cpp, via VAYU_ENGINE_SOURCE_DIR) and the app's vitest suite (app/src/services/codegen/prepare.conformance.test.ts). The rule is the engine's `apply_auth` (engine/src/http/auth_resolver.cpp): bearer, basic and an API key in a header are skipped when `headers` already holds that name, compared case-insensitively and whatever its value (an empty typed value still wins); an API key in the query is a URL parameter and is appended regardless. The snippet generators flatten auth in app/src/services/codegen/prepare.ts and would otherwise print the typed header and the auth one, two lines where Vayu sends one. Each case: `headers` (the request's typed headers, name -> value), `auth` (the auth block), `url` the request URL, and `expected`: `headers`, the [name, value] pairs that reach the wire in any order (a skipped auth header leaves the typed spelling of the name), and `url`. The app side renders a `basic` block that no typed header displaced as its `Authorization: Basic` pair before comparing, because a snippet keeps those credentials structured for -u, -a and auth=. The credentials in these cases are made up.

cases.name: a typed Authorization wins over bearer
a typed lower-case authorization wins over bearer
a typed lower-case authorization wins over basic
a typed Authorization with an empty value still wins over bearer
a typed header named like an API key in another case wins (x-key against X-Key)
a typed header named like an API key in another case wins (X-KEY against x-key)
an API key whose name no typed header carries is still written
a typed Authorization does not displace an API key under another name
an API key in the query is appended whatever a typed header of that name holds
an API key with no name writes nothing
bearer with no typed Authorization writes one
basic with no typed Authorization writes one
